evidence_items.locator: section Hallucination evaluations, text after Table 3

receipt.public_excerpt: More work is needed to understand hallucinations holistically, particularly in domains not covered by our evaluations (e.g., chemistry).

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's Table 3 gives SimpleQA hallucination rates of 0.61 for GPT-4o and 0.44 for o1-preview. Even OpenAI's newest, most heavily scaled models still hallucinated often.

receipt.public_excerpt: the AI research tools made by LexisNexis (Lexis+ AI) and Thomson Reuters (Westlaw AI-Assisted Research and Ask Practical Law AI) each hallucinate between 17% and 33% of the time.

evidence_items.explanation: Commercial RAG legal tools sold as hallucination-free still hallucinated 17–33% of the time in 2024. So RAG did not make hallucinations go away.

receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT returned partially or entirely incorrect responses on a hundred and fifty-three occasions

evidence_items.explanation: ChatGPT Search, built on GPT-4o with web retrieval, still made up wrong sources in most of 200 tests in November 2024.

unresolved_gaps: Hallucination rates vary a lot by task, and some benchmarks (such as summarization tests) show low single-digit rates. Those are still not zero.
